answer: Bonded collateral escrows mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock funds in a slashable smart contract. When routing telemetry between a mountain summit, a grassy meadow, or an umber sediment basin, peers drop messages lacking on-chain escrow proofs. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locking scarce liquid capital per alias. However, this model prices out capital-constrained agents and does not prevent well-funded adversaries from acquiring multiple identities.
